primary_claim: Matryoshka SAEs trained on Gemma-2-2B achieve worse reconstruction (MSE / variance explained) than standard BatchTopK SAEs but similar downstream cross-entropy loss, show dramatically lower feature-absorption rates (~0.03 vs up to ~0.29 for large BatchTopK SAEs) and feature-splitting, more disentangled latents (less shared information via meta-SAEs), and better targeted concept-erasure (TPP/SCR) performance, but show mixed results on k-sparse probing and only small differences in automated interpretability scores.

effect.metric: feature absorption rate (first-letter task, per Chanin et al. methodology)
effect.value: Matryoshka SAEs maintain absorption rates around 0.03 even as dictionary size increases, vs BatchTopK SAEs reaching approximately 0.29 at larger dictionary sizes

contradicts_or_qualifies: Independently parallels and cross-validates Noa Nabeshima's Matryoshka SAE work (zbebxYCqsryPALh8C), with architectural differences (fixed vs sampled group sizes, BatchTopK vs vanilla activation, no latent reordering)
stated_future_work: Qualitative investigation of feature absorption, splitting, or composition case studies comparing normal and Matryoshka SAEs
Investigate architectural tweaks: effect of latent sorting, random vs fixed group sizes, whether the smallest sub-SAE should get gradients from all losses
Further investigate why adding more latents to the sparse probing task hurts performance
Test whether the lower interpretability of later-group latents replicates with human judges rather than only automated interpretability
Hyperparameter investigations: best number of nested sub-SAEs and their sizes
limitations_stated: Matryoshka SAEs achieve worse reconstruction performance (MSE and variance explained) than standard BatchTopK SAEs
K-sparse probing results are mixed and confusing; unclear how to interpret them
Automated interpretability shows only small differences, and later-group latents are slightly less interpretable than BatchTopK
Only a single Matryoshka SAE was trained (not multiple seeds/configurations)
quote: Matryoshka SAEs show dramatically lower rates of feature absorption, feature splits and shared information between latents.
